papers.title: Testing the Pseudo-Dirac Nature of Atmospheric Neutrinos
papers.abstract: Pseudo-Dirac neutrinos are characterized by extremely small mass-squared differences between two nearly degenerate, strongly-mixed, active-sterile states. These differences are associated with new very-long oscillation lengths and provide a probe of the nature of neutrinos. Atmospheric neutrinos can probe these oscillations as they allow access to a broad range of baseline distances, from tens of kilometers to the Earth's diameter. We investigate the sensitivity of an experiment like the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE) to the pseudo-Dirac nature of neutrinos through measurements of the atmospheric neutrino flux. We concentrate on the modifications to the atmospheric neutrino energy and angular spectra induced by one new oscillation frequency associated with the $\nu_3$ state and determine the parameter space that can be probed with atmospheric neutrinos at a DUNE-like detector. We also comment on the sensitivity of these measurements to the sub-leading "solar" oscillations, which are also characterized by a relatively small mass-squared difference.
papers.reason: Investigates DUNE sensitivity to pseudo-Dirac atmospheric neutrino oscillations across baseline distances, squarely in the core neutrino phenomenology interest. [favorite author: Andre de Gouvea]

summary.tldr: DUNE atmospheric neutrinos can constrain pseudo-Dirac mass splittings $\Delta m^2_{33'}\gtrsim 10^{-4}\text{ eV}^2$, with sensitivity strongly governed by sub-GeV detector angular resolution and correlations with standard oscillation parameters.
summary.novel_idea: Focuses on atmospheric neutrinos at a DUNE-like LArTPC to probe the least-constrained pseudo-Dirac mass splitting $\Delta m^2_{33'}$ associated with the third mass eigenstate. It systematically quantifies how sub-GeV angular reconstruction performance and standard oscillation parameter profiling ($\theta_{23}, \Delta m^2_{31}$) impact experimental reach.
summary.method: Uses a 3+1 active-sterile maximal-mixing formalism for pseudo-Dirac neutrino propagation through a 5-layer PREM Earth model. Simulated atmospheric flux (Honda Homestake solar minimum) and GLoBES $^{40}\text{Ar}$ cross sections are evaluated for a 200 kt\cdot yr DUNE exposure across measured energy and zenith angle bins, profiling over NuFit global fit uncertainties.
key_results: A 200 kt\cdot yr DUNE exposure achieves a $3\sigma$ sensitivity limit of $\Delta m^2_{33'} \ge 2.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ eV}^2$ (dimensionless parameter $\epsilon \ge 4.0 \times 10^{-2}$) assuming a conservative $50^\circ$ sub-GeV angular resolution.
An optimistic $15^\circ$ sub-GeV angular resolution improves the $3\sigma$ reach to $\Delta m^2_{33'} \ge 6.0 \times 10^{-5}\text{ eV}^2$ ($\epsilon \ge 1.2 \times 10^{-2}$).
Profiling over uncertainties in $\theta_{23}$ and $\Delta m^2_{31}$ weakens the sensitivity due to correlations between $\epsilon$ and the atmospheric disappearance amplitude.
Atmospheric neutrinos provide very weak standalone sensitivity to solar parameters $\Delta m^2_{21}$ and $\sin^2\theta_{12}$, failing to rule out $\Delta m^2_{21}=0$ at $>2\sigma$.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to DUNE atmospheric oscillation analyses, low-energy LArTPC detector performance requirements, and BSM pseudo-Dirac neutrino searches, connecting event-by-event angular resolution to mass-splitting constraints.
summary.caveats: Assumes maximal active-sterile mixing ($\theta_{34}$ determined solely by pseudo-Dirac structure) and sets $\delta_{\text{CP}}=0^\circ$; sensitivity relies heavily on sub-1 GeV angular reconstruction capabilities.

papers.title: A framework for matrix-element-corrected QED antenna showers in hadron decays
papers.abstract: We present a general framework for the description of QED parton showers in hadron decays. The formalism is constructed in terms of coherent QED antennae with full dependence on particle masses and extends beyond the YFS approach by systematically incorporating spin-dependent (quasi)collinear single-unresolved limits to all orders. In addition, we incorporate corrections derived from tree-level matrix elements up to $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ and describe a generic procedure to obtain such matrix elements using FeynRules and MadGraph. We provide an explicit implementation of the method for decays involving pseudoscalar mesons and for decays of vectors and pseudoscalars into fermion-antifermion pairs, within the combined Pythia+Vincia parton-shower Monte Carlo framework, and compare the resulting QED emission spectra to those generated with Photos and Sherpa+Photons++ through the EvtGen generator.
papers.topic: QED Antenna Showers in Hadron Decays
papers.reason: Develops matrix-element-corrected QED antenna showers with mass dependence and spin correlations for Pythia/Vincia, closely aligning with generator and radiation modeling interests. [favorite author: Peter Skands]

summary.tldr: Presents a QED sector-antenna shower framework in Pythia/Vincia for hadron decays with full mass/spin dependence and automated matrix-element corrections up to $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$.
summary.novel_idea: Extends the Vincia antenna shower to generic hadron decays (spin-0, 1/2, 1) incorporating coherent soft-multipole eikonals and spin-dependent collinear DGLAP limits. It also establishes an automated FeynRules and MadGraph pipeline to introduce up to second-order tree-level matrix-element corrections (MECs).
summary.method: Formulates mass-dependent sector antennae in Vincia for QED radiation off charged hadrons. Incorporates tree-level ME corrections using an automated EFT toolchain, interfaces with EvtGen for hadron decay generation, and compares predictions against Photos, Pythia, and Sherpa/Photons++.
key_results: Second-order $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2)$ ME corrections consistently increase average emitted photon energy by $1-3\%$ relative to uncorrected showers.

For fully charged three-body decays (e.g. $D^+ \to \pi^+\pi^-\pi^+$), the simplified maximal-screening dipole option overestimates average energy loss by $5-20\%$ compared to the full coherent multipole shower.
Demonstrates linear multi-threaded CPU speedup in EvtGen via thread-local Vincia instances, avoiding the thread-locking bottlenecks of Photos and Photons++.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides a modernized QED parton shower tool in Pythia/Vincia for hadron decay chains, offering useful insights into soft/collinear photon radiation modeling and generator multithreading efficiency.
summary.caveats: Hadronic form factors are currently set to unity (point-like approximation); spin-3/2 hadrons are treated as spin-1/2; tree-level MEC plugins are currently limited to scalar and vector decay channels.

papers.title: Wigner distribution modeling of nuclear state in NuWro Monte Carlo event generator
papers.abstract: We develop a method to use the Wigner distribution (WD) description of the nuclear initial state of $^{12}$C, $^{16}$O, $^{40}$Ar, and $^{56}$Fe for quasielastic scattering in the NuWro Monte Carlo event generator. We propose two different algorithms to deal with the problem of negative values of the WDs. In our treatment, finite-nucleus WDs provide a correlation between the position and the momentum of bound nucleons that is very different from what is assumed in the standard approaches based on the Fermi gas model and spectral functions. We show that the use of WDs leads to effects that can be measured experimentally and may be relevant for future neutrino oscillation experiments.
papers.reason: Implements finite-nucleus Wigner distributions for quasielastic scattering in the NuWro Monte Carlo generator, directly targeting core neutrino-nucleus interaction and generator modeling interests. [favorite author: Jan Sobczyk]

summary.tldr: Develops a shell-resolved nuclear Wigner distribution initial state in NuWro for quasielastic scattering, handling negative quasiprobability regions via weighted and unweighted sampling and predicting measurable FSI effects.
summary.novel_idea: Introduces quantum shell-resolved Wigner distributions (WDs) into a neutrino Monte Carlo event generator (NuWro), capturing position-momentum correlations of bound nucleons beyond the local Fermi gas approximation. It introduces two practical algorithms (signed weighted sampling and non-negative coarse-graining) to overcome negative WD values.
summary.method: Computes shell-resolved WDs from mean-field bound states for $^{12}\text{C}$, $^{16}\text{O}$, $^{40}\text{Ar}$, and $^{56}\text{Fe}$. Implements signed-branch sampling with event weights, as well as a coarse-graining algorithm that preserves the exact momentum marginal. Connects initial nucleon position/momentum to NuWro's primary vertex and intranuclear cascade (INC) FSI.
key_results: Inclusive cross sections in the WD framework strictly reduce to the plane-wave impulse approximation (PWIA) and remain non-negative despite negative initial WD regions.

Coarse-grained unweighted sampling introduces minimal spatial distortion ($\sim 3\%$ for $^{12}\text{C}/^{16}\text{O}$ and $\sim 7\%$ for $^{40}\text{Ar}/^{56}\text{Fe}$) while exactly reproducing the original shell momentum distribution.

Position-momentum correlations and shell-dependent interaction points shift the relative height of the $1p_{3/2}$ and $1s_{1/2}$ missing-energy peaks in JSNS2 mono-energetic $\nu_m\text{-}^{12}\text{C}$ interactions by $7-10\%$.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly impacts core neutrino-nucleus interaction modeling, MC event generators (NuWro, GENIE, GiBUU), initial-state nuclear structure implementation, and exclusive final-state predictions (INC FSI, missing energy in argon/carbon).
summary.caveats: Uses shell separation energies with delta-function binding energy assignments rather than realistic continuous spectral functions; initial nucleons are off-shell according to default NuWro kinematics.

papers.title: Quark-mass dependence of two-nucleon scattering
papers.abstract: Understanding how the properties of the visible Universe depend on the parameters of the Standard Model of particle physics requires \emph{ab initio} theoretical computations. To that end, we investigate the quark-mass dependence of low-energy nucleon-nucleon scattering in the deuteron and dineutron channels. We perform lattice-QCD calculations at pion masses $M_\pi\approx 200$ and $280$ MeV and compare their results to phenomenology at the physical point and to a previous calculation at $M_\pi\approx 710$ MeV. Scattering amplitudes, phase shifts, and threshold parameters are determined from finite-volume spectra using quantization conditions that explicitly incorporate long-distance effects from one-pion exchange. We analyze the pion-mass dependence of scattering lengths and effective ranges using chiral effective field theory with Weinberg and Kaplan-Savage-Wise power countings. From this, we estimate the pion-mass derivatives of the inverse scattering lengths and binding momentum, at the physical point. Both power countings indicate that the deuteron unbinds near $M_\pi\approx 220$ MeV.

papers.reason: Performs ab initio lattice-QCD calculations of low-energy nucleon-nucleon scattering across quark masses, directly connecting to nuclear EFT and neutrino-nucleus inputs.

summary.tldr: Lattice QCD calculations of nucleon-nucleon scattering at $M_\pi \approx 200, 280\text{ MeV}$ matched to chiral EFT predict that the deuteron unbinds near $M_\pi \approx 220\text{ MeV}$.
summary.novel_idea: Presents lattice QCD calculations of two-nucleon ($^1S_0$ dineutron and $^3S_1-^3D_1$ deuteron) scattering at light pion masses ($M_\pi \approx 200, 280\text{ MeV}$) analyzed via quantization conditions with explicit long-range one-pion exchange, enabling chiral EFT extrapolations of $NN$ observables to physical quark masses.
summary.method: Performs $N_f=2+1$ Wilson-clover lattice QCD simulations using distillation and multi-hadron operator bases. Extracts energy levels via generalized eigenvalue problems and maps them to scattering phase shifts using plane-wave and relativistic quantization conditions. Fits pion-mass dependence using Weinberg and KSW power-counting chiral EFTs.
key_results: Both Weinberg and KSW chiral EFT power countings predict that the deuteron becomes unbound near $M_\pi \approx 220\text{ MeV}$.
The pion-mass derivative of the inverse deuteron scattering length at the physical point is determined as $d(a^{-1}_{^3S_1})/dM_\pi = -0.47(16)$ (Weinberg) and $-0.46(24)$ (KSW).
Effective ranges $r_0$ for both $^1S_0$ and $^3S_1$ channels show very weak pion-mass dependence between $M_\pi \approx 138\text{ MeV}$ and $280\text{ MeV}$.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides crucial $ab\ initio$ inputs for nuclear chiral EFTs, lattice QCD nuclear forces, nuclear binding sensitivity to Standard Model parameters, and nuclear structure calculations.
summary.caveats: Neglects strange-quark mass variations across ensembles; KSW power counting displays a relatively large NLO/LO ratio $\mathcal{A}_0/\mathcal{A}_{-1}$, signaling potential scheme-dependent convergence challenges.

papers.title: QED corrections to $e^+e^-\to\pi^+\pi^-(\gamma)$ with amplitude-level resummation
papers.abstract: We present QED corrections to $e^+e^-\to\pi^+\pi^-(\gamma)$ in two independent Monte Carlo event generators, KKMC and SHERPA, for point-like scalar pions dressed with the pion form factor. All-order soft-photon exponentiation is combined with exact one- and two-photon tree amplitudes, the complete one-loop correction including the initial-final boxes with coherent interference, and at second order the photonic two-loop vertices and the exact one-loop correction to one-photon emission. At first order their fiducial cross sections agree to $\lesssim0.04\%$ and their distributions within statistical precision. The second-order band is $\sim0.005\%$ for CMD, $\sim0.4\%$ at $4$ GeV and $\sim0.9\%$ at $10$ GeV. Theory nuisance parameters estimate missing higher orders, and we construct a new rule for treating radiative return, where first-order corrections are of order one.
papers.reason: High-precision QED corrections and resummation in KKMC and SHERPA for e+e- pion production, relevant to advanced event generator physics. [favorite author: Frank Krauss]

summary.tldr: Matches YFS soft-photon resummation with exact 1- and 2-photon matrix elements for $e^+e^-\to\pi^+	ext{\pi}^-(\gamma)$, achieving sub-0.04% generator agreement and introducing theory nuisance parameters for QED uncertainties.
summary.novel_idea: Constructs amplitude-level YFS soft-photon exponentiation matched to exact NLO/NNLO-like real/virtual scalar QED matrix elements in two independent event generators (KKMC/CEEX and SHERPA/ACRAIC). It establishes a novel theory-nuisance-parameter framework to systematically estimate missing higher-order QED uncertainties.
summary.method: Models pions as sQED scalars dressed with the STRONG2020 pion form factor (F$\times$sQED vs. GVMD loop prescriptions). Computes complete 1-loop virtuals, 1-loop real-virtuals, and exact 1- and 2-photon tree amplitudes. Compares fiducial cross sections across five experimental setups (CMD, KLOE-I, KLOE-II, BESIII, B) and against BabaYaga@NLO.
key_results: KKMC and SHERPA fiducial cross sections agree to $\le 0.04\%$ at $\mathcal{O}(\alpha)$ and $\le 0.03\%$ at $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2 L)$ across all experimental setups.
Theory nuisance parameter bands at $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^2 L)$ are $\sim 0.005\%$ for CMD, $\sim 0.1\%$ for KLOE-I, $\sim 0.4\%$ for BESIII, and $\sim 0.9\%$ for B-factories.
Using GVMD instead of point-like loops inside virtual diagrams shifts the forward-backward asymmetry in CMD-3 kinematics by up to $\sim 1\%$ near the $\rho$ peak.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides state-of-the-art QED radiative corrections and theoretical uncertainty quantification for $e^+e^-\to\pi^+\pi^-$, essential for hadronic vacuum polarization (HVP) input to $(g-2)_\mu$ and precision electron scattering analyses.
summary.caveats: Pion loop structure relies on effective sQED/GVMD form-factor modeling rather than full dispersive hadronic QED; non-logarithmic 2-loop initial-final boxes and $\mathcal{O}(\alpha^3)$ corrections are estimated via nuisance parameters rather than explicitly calculated.

papers.title: Constraining $U(1)_{L_\mu-L_\tau}$ Model with Dark Matter Using Relic Density and $N_{\rm eff}$ Bounds
papers.abstract: We study thermal Dirac dark matter in the gauged $U(1)_{L_\mu-L_\tau}$ model, focusing on resonant annihilation near the $Z'$ pole. We determine the parameter space that satisfies the Planck relic density bound while remaining consistent with collider, astrophysical, and laboratory searches. MeV-scale dark matter and the $Z'$ mediator decouple near the active neutrino decoupling temperature; entropy injection into the neutrino bath modifies $T_\nu/T_\gamma$, leading to a shift in the effective number of relativistic species, $N_{\rm eff}$. Incorporating the coupled temperature evolution alongside the Planck 2018 limit on $N_{\rm eff}$, we find that the viable parameter space is restricted to a narrow mass window of $M_{Z'} \sim 30\text{--}50\text{ MeV}$ with $g' \simeq 10^{-7}-10^{-6}$, well within reach of upcoming fixed-target experiments such as SHiP and LDMX.
papers.reason: Examines MeV-scale dark matter and Z' mediators in L_mu - L_tau models, neutrino decoupling, and Neff bounds relevant for SHiP and LDMX.

Thermal Dirac dark matter in a gauged $U(1)_{L_

The authors solve coupled Boltzmann equations for the thermal yields and bath temperatures, using a resonance tuning parameter $ rac{M_{Z'}-2m_{
u,	ext{DM}}}{M_{Z'}}	o  rac{1}{2}	ext{or} rac{1}{10}$, and compare the surviving parameter space against Planck relic density and $N_{m eff}$ limits as well as laboratory and astrophysical exclusions.

summary.why_it_matters: Directly relevant for BSM phenomenology at neutrino experiments, illustrating how neutrino-portal dark sectors and associated effects on $N_{m eff}$ and neutrino baths tie into accelerator searches like SHiP.
summary.caveats: Tree-level kinetic mixing is set to zero (only loop-induced mixing is retained), and a full phase-space treatment of the resonant cross section at smaller tuning parameters is left for future work.

papers.title: Linking chiral nuclear forces to light-ion collisions: a global sensitivity analysis
papers.abstract: Ultrarelativistic $^{16}$O+$^{16}$O and $^{20}$Ne+$^{20}$Ne collisions recently performed at the Large Hadron Collider have imaged quadrupole and octupole correlations between nucleons through the collective flow of emitted hadrons. We establish a quantitative link between these correlations and the low-energy constants (LECs) that enter chiral inter-nucleon interactions. Emulators built using the subspace-projected coupled-cluster method enable a global sensitivity analysis of the ground-state quadrupole mean-square eccentricity, revealing that quadrupole correlations respond linearly and additively to all 16 LECs at next-to-next-to-leading order in the chiral expansion. The sensitivities differ markedly in $^{16}$O and $^{20}$Ne, and are complementary to those of the binding energy and charge radius, the bulk observables to which nuclear interactions are typically calibrated. In particular, $^{20}$Ne collisions dominantly probe the spin-orbit part of two-nucleon interactions. Soft-particle correlations in light-ion collisions thus constitute a new type of data to study nuclear forces and their emergence from quantum chromodynamics.
papers.reason: Global sensitivity analysis linking chiral nuclear forces (LECs) to ultrarelativistic light-ion collisions and nucleon correlations, highly relevant for ab initio nuclear theory intersections.

summary.tldr: A global sensitivity analysis using subspace-projected coupled-cluster emulators establishes that quadrupole correlations probed by light-ion collisions respond linearly and additively to all 16 LECs in chiral EFT.
summary.novel_idea: The paper quantitatively bridges TeV-scale soft-particle correlations in ultrarelativistic $^{16}	ext{O}+^{16}	ext{O}$ and $^{20}	ext{Ne}+^{20}	ext{Ne}$ collisions at the LHC with underlying ab initio chiral nuclear forces, demonstrating that quadrupole moments probe independent combinations of LECs compared to binding energies and radii.
summary.method: Ground-state wave functions for $^{16}	ext{O}$ and $^{20}	ext{Ne}$ are computed using coupled-cluster theory (CCSD and angular-momentum-projected CC) with the NNLOsat Hamiltonian, while emulators based on eigenvector continuation facilitate a Saltelli global sensitivity analysis with over $5	imes 10^5$ evaluations to compute first-order Sobol indices for 16 LECs.
key_results: First-order Sobol indices sum to $0.99	ext{--}1.00$ for all studied observables, indicating a systematically additive response.

In $^{20}	ext{Ne}$, quadrupole correlations $ eta_2^2$ are dominated by the $^{3}P_2$ contact LEC ($S_1 = 0.82$), with about 70% of the $P$-wave sensitivity originating from the two-nucleon spin-orbit interaction.
In $^{16}	ext{O}$, $ eta_2^2$ is led by the subleading $^{3}S_1$ contact ($S_1 = 0.49$) and LO $^{3}S_1$ contact ($S_1 = 0.20$), with the $^{3}P_2$ main effect being negligible ($S_1 = 0.005$).
The gradient of $ eta_2^2$ in LEC space lies $38^{ho}$ ($54^{ho}$) outside the energy-radius plane in $^{20}	ext{Ne}$ ($^{16}	ext{O}$).
summary.why_it_matters: Highly relevant for ab initio nuclear theory and electroweak response calculations, providing a novel data-driven path to constrain inter-nucleon forces and low-energy constants using high-energy collider data.
summary.caveats: Parity breaking was not included in the $^{20}	ext{Ne}$ reference state, making the present octupole ($ eta_3^2$) analysis preliminary until parity-restoring frameworks are implemented.

papers.title: DIS-secting the universe with high-energy neutrinos
papers.abstract: We revisit the impact of electroweak (EW) radiative corrections on the kinematic distributions of charged leptons in neutrino-induced charged-current (CC) deep inelastic scattering (DIS). These corrections are particularly relevant for observables sensitive to collinear photon radiation, such as the energy spectrum of high-energy muons detected in neutrino telescopes. To study these effects, we implement full next-to-leading order (NLO) EW corrections to CC DIS in a flexible Monte Carlo framework, supplemented with higher-order logarithmically enhanced final-state QED radiation and coherent scattering contributions. We compare our results to exclusive NLO QCD plus parton shower (PS) predictions obtained with an existing $\texttt{POWHEG-BOX}$ event generator, examining different PS models and settings. Based on this comparison, we provide recommendations for the use of the $\texttt{POWHEG-BOX}$ event generator in experimental analyses. We further assess the impact of radiative corrections on the correlation between the observed muon energy and the incoming neutrino energy, and on the mean inelasticity averaged over a realistic neutrino flux. These corrections can exceed $10\%$, and above about $10^4\,{\rm GeV}$ they receive sizeable contributions from photon-initiated and coherent $W$-boson production, which are not included in the event generator.
papers.reason: Directly evaluates NLO electroweak and QED radiative corrections for high-energy neutrino-nucleus charged-current DIS, highly relevant for neutrino telescopes.

summary.tldr: Implementing full NLO electroweak corrections and QED final-state radiation for neutrino-nucleus DIS shows that radiative corrections exceed 10% and significantly distort charged-lepton energy spectra in high-energy neutrino telescopes.
summary.novel_idea: The authors systematically compare fixed-order NLO QCD+EW calculations with POWHEG-BOX NLO+PS predictions, demonstrating that using the hadronic COM energy $s$ rather than the partonic hard scale $	ilde{s}_{12}$ in LL fragmentation functions overestimates QED radiation by roughly 50% at ultra-high energies.
summary.method: Evaluated using a dedicated fixed-order Monte Carlo program incorporating dipole subtraction for NLO QCD and EW corrections, lepton fragmentation functions up to $ho(ho^2)$, coherent and diffractive $W$-boson production, and benchmarking against POWHEG-BOX v2 interfaced with Pythia 8.3.
key_results: NLO EW corrections to inclusive neutrino-DIS cross sections are at the percent level, but reach up to $+20ho$ for the flux-averaged mean inelasticity $ angle y  angle$ at $10^9	ext{ GeV}$ under an atmospheric neutrino flux.
Photon-induced and coherent $W$-boson production contribute sizeably above $10^4	ext{ GeV}$, affecting flavour-dependent CC DIS cross sections.
Setting the LL FSR scale to the partonic hard scale $	ilde{s}_{12} = x s$ instead of $s$ resolves a major overestimation present in previous literature estimates.
summary.why_it_matters:
Essential for high-energy neutrino telescope experiments (IceCube, KM3NeT, GRAND) and forward physics facilities (FASER$
u$, SHiP) where percent-level interaction modeling and precise muon/neutrino energy reconstruction are required.
summary.caveats: Detector-specific reconstruction effects and emulsion/scintillator resolutions are omitted, leaving a dedicated detector simulation to future experimental studies.

papers.title: Signatures of Neutrinophilic Pion Dark Matter
papers.abstract: We study the phenomenology of pion dark matter coupled to neutrinos in a confining sector that dynamically generates both small neutrino masses and dark matter mass from gauge confinement. Dark matter semi-annihilation to active neutrinos or annihilation to light sterile neutrinos can reproduce the observed relic abundance through thermal freeze-out while satisfying constraints from self-interactions. In the first scenario, semi-annihilations of sub-GeV dark matter in the galactic halo produce a flux of antineutrinos which can provide a viable interpretation for the mild electron antineutrino excess reported by the Super-Kamiokande collaboration. We assess the potential of the JUNO detector to test this interpretation. In the second scenario, light sterile neutrinos can leave signatures through displaced vertex searches at accelerator facilities.
papers.reason: Studies sub-GeV pion dark matter coupled to neutrinos via semi-annihilations explaining Super-K antineutrino excesses and testable at JUNO.

summary.tldr: Neutrinophilic dark pion dark matter from a confining hidden sector can explain the Super-Kamiokande electron antineutrino excess via semi-annihilations while satisfying cosmological relic density and self-interaction bounds.
summary.novel_idea: The framework dynamically generates both small neutrino masses (via an inverse seesaw mechanism tied to a confining gauge sector) and composite dark matter, utilizing a light pseudo-scalar mediator to enable semi-annihilations into neutrinos without violating self-interaction or BBN constraints.

papers.title: Construction and performance evaluation of a meter-scale monolithic scintillator tracker with embedded scatterers
papers.abstract: A meter-scale Fiber-Readout mOnolithic and Scatterer-embedded scintillator Tracker (FROST) was constructed and operated in the NINJA experiment to enable muon-track matching between the nuclear emulsion detectors and the downstream muon detector. The detector consists of a 1.32 m $\times$ 1.40 m plastic scintillator plate assembled from optically bonded scatterer-embedded plates, with wavelength-shifting fibers arranged at a pitch of 10 mm. During J-PARC neutrino-beam operation, FROST achieved a data acquisition efficiency of 99.59% and a detection efficiency of 99.946$\pm$0.006% for selected neutrino-induced muons well within the active area. A position reconstruction method based on the light-yield distribution was developed for both single- and multi-particle events. In a neutrino-interaction simulation, muon position resolutions of 1.77 mm and 1.61 mm were achieved in the two orthogonal readout directions, assuming correct muon identification. Using a beam-data sample dominated by single-muon events, upper limits on the position resolution of 2.20 mm and 2.03 mm were obtained for track angles below 20{\deg}. These results demonstrate that the FROST concept can be scaled up to a meter-scale active area while maintaining high detection efficiency and a position resolution well below the readout pitch under actual experimental conditions.
papers.reason: Constructs and evaluates a meter-scale monolithic scintillator tracker (FROST) with embedded scatterers for neutrino experiments like NINJA and J-PARC.

summary.tldr: A meter-scale Fiber-Readout monolithic and Scatterer-embedded scintillator Tracker (FROST) was constructed for the NINJA experiment, achieving 99.59% DAQ efficiency and a muon position resolution well below its 10 mm readout pitch.
summary.novel_idea: Scaling the FROST concept to a meter-scale active area ($1.32	ext{ m} 	imes 1.40	ext{ m}$) via optically bonded scatterer-embedded scintillator plates and developing a multi-particle position reconstruction algorithm based on channel light-yield distributions.
summary.method: Assembled 24 custom Kuraray scatterer-embedded plates using EJ-500 optical cement, integrated WLS fibers at a 10 mm pitch read out by 272 SiPM channels, tuned Geant4 optical parameters using cosmic-ray data, and evaluated performance with J-PARC neutrino beam data and sand-muons.
key_results: Achieved a data acquisition efficiency of 99.59% during the J-PARC neutrino beam run ($1.0217	imes 10^{21}$ POT recorded).
Measured a muon detection efficiency of $99.946ho 0.006ho$ for selected events well within the active area.
In neutrino-interaction simulations, muon position resolutions of $1.77	ext{ mm}$ ($x$) and $1.61	ext{ mm}$ ($y$) were achieved.
Using beam data dominated by single muons with track angles below $20^{ho}$, upper limits on position resolution of $2.20	ext{ mm}$ ($x$) and $2.03	ext{ mm}$ ($y$) were obtained.
summary.why_it_matters: Highly relevant for neutrino-nucleus interaction experiments (NINJA, T2K) requiring fine spatial resolution and high tracking efficiency without proliferating readout channels.
summary.caveats: Multi-particle position resolution could not be directly verified using beam data due to limited multi-track statistics, relying instead on Monte Carlo simulations.

papers.title: Partial-wave decomposition of the $p$--$^{5}_{\Lambda}\mathrm{He}$ correlation function: a femtoscopic route to the $^{6}_{\Lambda}\mathrm{Li}$ resonance
papers.abstract: The hypernucleus $^{6}_{\Lambda}\mathrm{Li}$ is unbound against proton emission, so its resonances appear in the low-momentum $p$--$^{5}_{\Lambda}\mathrm{He}$ correlation function, which femtoscopy can measure. We compute this correlation function in an $\alpha+\Lambda$ folding model of $^{5}_{\Lambda}\mathrm{He}$: phenomenological $p\alpha$ and $p\Lambda$ interactions are averaged over the internal $\alpha$--$\Lambda$ motion, and a single $\Lambda N$ strength factor is fixed by the measured $^{6}_{\Lambda}\mathrm{He}$ binding energy. The model places the $^{6}_{\Lambda}\mathrm{Li}$ $1^{-}$ state at $E_{R}=0.60^{+0.11}_{-0.10}$~MeV with $\Gamma=0.18\pm0.05$~MeV and produces a pronounced peak in $C(k^{*})$ near $31~\mathrm{MeV}/c$. The predicted peak position, $k^{*}_{\rm peak}=\sqrt{2\mu E_{R}}=30.8\pm2.6~\mathrm{MeV}/c$, is uncertain mainly because of the measured $B_\Lambda(^{6}_{\Lambda}\mathrm{He})$, not because of the $\Lambda N$ interaction. An exact partial-wave decomposition shows that the $P$ wave accounts for the entire enhancement over the Coulomb baseline, $79\%$ of it from the $1^{-}$ channel. A Lednick\'y--Lyuboshitz analysis restricted to $S$ waves therefore cannot describe this system. The maximum of the $1^{-}$ channel lies within $1\%$ of $k^{*}_{\rm peak}$, but the unresolved $2^{-}$ state and the momentum resolution shift the measured maximum upward by $2.4~\mathrm{MeV}/c$ at $\sigma_{k^{*}}=3~\mathrm{MeV}/c$.
papers.reason: Computes p-5LambdaHe correlation functions and Lambda N interactions via femtoscopy, highly relevant for low-energy nuclear physics and final-state interactions.

papers.title: Power corrections to heavy-quark spin correlations in small-$x$ deep-inelastic scattering
papers.abstract: Heavy-quark spin correlations in small-$x$ deep-inelastic scattering receive corrections beyond the back-to-back limit. For a rotationally symmetric target at leading power, the target dependence cancels from the normalized spin density matrix after full azimuthal averaging, for fixed kinematics and spin axes related by transverse light-front boosts. We calculate the first nonvanishing correction at tree level for finite quark mass and finite $N_c$ in a homogeneous Gaussian target. The expansion through fourth order in the dipole sizes includes logarithms, contact terms and all interference contributions at that order. Comparison with the improved transverse-momentum-dependent approximation separates kinematic corrections from terms with additional insertions of the target current. Numerical integration of the unexpanded Gaussian kernel tests the approximation at 28 parameter points. Spin correlations differ between the two targets in all 12 kinematic comparisons; in one comparison both spin states remain separable. At fixed photon virtuality, the leading large-$P$ behavior of the fourth-order correction to the normalized transverse spin state is generically proportional to $m\ln P/P^3$. We also compare two fixed Gaussian targets using unpolarized momentum distributions and joint spin measurements. For a purely transverse photon, three narrow momentum bins and an ideal measurement of both spins along the common quark-momentum axis defined by the light-front boost, spin information adds 3.5-3.7 percent to the expected log likelihood ratio after the overall normalization is fitted. This increase depends on the spin analyzing power and bin selection. The calculation establishes a model-dependent effect, rather than an experimental sensitivity prediction.
papers.reason: Calculates power corrections to heavy-quark spin correlations in small-x DIS beyond the back-to-back limit, matching deep interests in DIS and spin dynamics.

papers.title: Manifestation of scale symmetry in nuclear medium
papers.abstract: This memorial tribute to Mannque Rho focuses on the role of scale symmetry in baryonic matter, especially on its profound influence on the possible resolution of the ``quenched $g_A$" problem in the Gamow-Teller transition of nuclei, the pseudoconformal structure of dense nuclear matter and the origin of the peak of sound velocity of nuclear matter. The discussion is based on the genuine dilaton scenario, anchored on the Crewther-Tunstall infrared fixed point, which provides a unified framework where scale symmetry---broken explicitly by the QCD trace anomaly---can be spontaneously broken, yielding the scalar $f_0(500)$ as a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson. In nuclear medium, this scenario serves as a natural foundation of the Brown-Rho scaling---a relation that has been central to nuclear physics for over three decades. The sound velocity of nuclear matter exhibits a characteristic peak at intermediate densities arising from the kink behavior of the dilaton field, a unique signature of scale symmetry realization that distinguishes the dilaton-compensated effective theory from conventional Walecka-type models. At higher densities, the approach to the dilaton-limit fixed point produces pseudo-conformal behavior with sound velocity $v_s^2 = 1/3$ saturating from below at $n \gtrsim 3n_0$, while the trace of the energy-momentum tensor remains nonzero. The framework also provides a natural resolution of the long-standing ``quenched $g_A$" problem, demonstrating that nuclear correlations, not fundamental quenching, account for the effective axial coupling approaching unity. The continuity from the unitary limit at low density to the dilaton limit at high density suggests a pervasive role for scale symmetry in nuclear dynamics across all density regimes.
papers.reason: Discusses scale symmetry, Brown-Rho scaling, the quenched gA problem, and sound velocity peaks in dense nuclear matter.

papers.title: Chiral invariant mass and scale symmetry in dense matter from a dilaton compensated parity doublet model
papers.abstract: In the parity doublet model the nucleon mass includes a chiral invariant part $m_0$, which is conventionally assumed to be medium independent. We promote this assumption to a dynamical question by making the model scale invariant using a dilaton compensator $\chi$, so that the effective chiral invariant mass $m_{\rm inv}^\ast = m_0\tilde\chi$, with $\tilde\chi = \chi/f_\chi$, responds to the partial restoration of scale symmetry in the medium. We fit the model parameters by using vacuum spectra, nuclear matter properties, and NICER mass--radius posteriors---with the hadronic equation of state connected to 2+1-flavor Nambu--Jona-Lasinio quark matter by an interpolation. The best fit gives $m_0 = 657$ MeV, a maximum neutron-star mass of $2.30\,M_\odot$ and $R_{1.4} = 12.22$ km, with the mass--radius sequence passing through all three NICER credible regions. The resulting tidal deformabilities, $\Lambda_{1.4} = 387$ and $\tilde\Lambda = 463$, are consistent with GW170817 measurements. The in-medium analysis separates the two restorations: at the hadron--quark matching density the chiral condensate falls to $56\%$ of its vacuum value, while the dilaton decreases only to $94\%$, so the nucleon arrives at the matching density with $90\%$ of its mass carried by the invariant part. The order parameters of chiral and scale symmetries organize the in-medium probes, making the $\omega$ an almost pure probe of scale symmetry and the $\rho$ of chiral restoration, which gives us a clue on the origin of hadron mass.
papers.reason: Applies a dilaton-compensated parity doublet model to dense nuclear matter, examining chiral invariant mass, neutron star properties, and in-medium scaling.

papers.title: Probing Dark Matter-Electron Scattering with the Central Molecular Zone
papers.abstract: The Central Molecular Zone, a dense and gas-rich region surrounding the Galactic Center, hosts numerous dense molecular gas cores that provide unique environments to probe dark matter interactions. Among these, the IRS 13E3 cluster is one of the closest to the Galactic Center and one of the most extensively studied. We show that dark matter-electron scattering can substantially ionize molecular hydrogen (H$_2$) in the IRS 13E3 core, contributing to the ionization rate in conjunction with standard cosmic rays. Using the ionization rate inferred from H$_3^+$ observations of the central parsecs, we derive constraints on heavy and ultralight dark photon mediators, a heavy leptophilic mediator, and electric dipole moment interactions in the strongly interacting regime, where terrestrial searches are limited by the overburden problem. Our results highlight the potential of dense molecular cores near the Galactic Center as promising targets for constraining dark matter interactions with future observations.
papers.reason: Calculates dark matter scattering in the Central Molecular Zone, relevant for dark matter searches overlapping with astrophysical probes.

papers.title: Searches for electroweak singlets at future plasma wakefield colliders
papers.reason: Studies Higgs portal scalar sensitivity at future plasma wakefield and muon-class colliders.

papers.title: Constraining the parameter space of a singlet down-type vector-like quark
papers.abstract: We consider a minimal New Physics scenario in which the Standard Model is extended by singlet down-type vector-like quark(VLQ). We constrain its parameter space using the measured branching ratios for $B_s \to \mu^+ \mu^-$, $B \to X_s \mu^+ \mu^-$ and $B \to X_s \gamma$, which are all consistent with Standard Model predictions. Besides considering the tree-level flavor-changing-neutral-current amplitude allowed in this NP scenario, we account for a Higgs--VLQ loop amplitude and show that their resulting interference drives the VLQ mass into the discovery reach via direct searches at the LHC. We also examine the implications of this minimal NP scenario for the rare $B \to K \nu \bar{\nu}$ decay where there is a persistent tension between the SM prediction and the Belle II measurements.
papers.topic: Singlet Vector-Like Quarks and B Decays
papers.reason: Constrains vector-like quarks using B-meson decays and rare neutral current / neutrino channels (B to K nu nubar).

papers.title: The Colour Glass Condensate
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive introduction to the Colour Glass Condensate (CGC) effective theory, a first-principles framework for hadronic interactions in high-energy Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) at large parton densities. The focus is on the underlying physical picture and associated emergent phenomena, such as gluon saturation, transverse momentum broadening, and geometric scaling. We introduce the key components of the CGC formalism: the semiclassical approximation for dense gluon systems at saturation, the nonlinear JIMWLK equation governing the energy evolution of multi-gluon correlations, and its mean-field approximation, the BK equation. The formalism is illustrated through applications to selected "dilute-dense" processes, namely high-energy electron-nucleus and proton-nucleus collisions. Finally, we briefly discuss advanced topics including higher-order radiative corrections, the Langevin formulation of the JIMWLK equation, and the emergence of transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) factorisation from the CGC effective theory.
papers.reason: Comprehensive introduction to the CGC effective theory, saturation, and multi-parton interactions relevant to high-energy QCD.

papers.title: Generalized parton distributions of the nucleon in the chiral quark soliton model II: Chiral anomaly mediation in the polarized GPDs
papers.abstract: We calculate the polarized flavor-singlet generalized parton distributions (GPDs) $\widetilde H^{u+d}$ and $\widetilde E^{u+d}$ in the chiral quark soliton model at nonzero skewness and momentum transfer. Results are obtained with and without a singlet pseudoscalar meson $\eta_0$, whose mass is generated by the chiral anomaly. Relative to the pion-only model, the singlet field introduces a sizable contribution to $\widetilde E^{u+d}$ in the ERBL region but only a minor correction to $\widetilde H^{u+d}$. An explicit meson-exchange term qualitatively accounts for this contrast and displays the anticipated singlet pole. When the anomaly-induced mass is set to zero, the pole becomes massless, and the exchange term dominates $\widetilde E^{u+d}$ at small momentum transfer. These findings demonstrate how anomalous singlet-meson dynamics leaves distinct signatures in the polarized GPDs of the nucleon.
papers.topic: GPDs in Chiral Quark Soliton Model
papers.reason: Calculates polarized GPDs including singlet pseudoscalar meson and chiral anomaly effects in the chiral quark soliton model.

papers.title: On the Nucleon Effective Mass in Neutron Stars Cooling
papers.abstract: The cooling of neutrons stars, which are composed of ultra-high-density nuclear matter, strongly depends on the equation of state because the dominant cooling sources are neutrinos produced in their interiors. Here, we investigate the cooling properties of neutron stars, focusing on effective nucleon masses, whose impacts have been recently examined in supernova explosion and proto-neutron star cooling. The uncertainties of effective masses originate from the difference in the attractive interaction of scalar meson and the definition of the Dirac and Landau masses. At first, we employ so-called Walecka models that allow these two masses to be introduced within a unified framework and evaluate the resulting cooling curves. Based on the Walecka model, we compute the emissivity of the neutrons and the direct Urca process and their cooling curves. We demonstrate that the Dirac and Landau masses affect cooling of massive neutron stars, although most previous cooling simulations do not distinguish them. We also perform cooling simulations with two realistic equation of states based on relativistic mean-field (RMF) theory, whose differences arise from properties of only effective masses among characteristic parameters. These results are broadly consistent with those obtained from the Walecka models, indicating that the treatment of effective nucleon masses may be an important source of uncertainty in neutron-star cooling.
papers.reason: Investigates how Dirac and Landau nucleon effective masses affect neutron star cooling via neutrino emission and Urca processes.

papers.title: Latest $\nu$s from the Earliest Galaxies: Probing neutrino self-interactions with JWST
papers.abstract: Our Universe serves as a complementary laboratory for particle physics interactions. One intriguing possibility is that neutrinos may have beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) self-interactions, which can delay their free streaming and have an observable effect across different redshifts. Such interactions can induce scale-dependent changes in the matter power spectrum. The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has opened up a new window onto the early Universe by discovering a large population of high-redshift galaxies up to $z \sim 15$ and various probable galaxy candidates at even higher redshifts, between $z \sim 15-30$. Such high-redshift observations can probe the matter power spectrum on small scales, since structure formation is hierarchical and the structures hosting these high-redshift galaxies are therefore expected to be small. We, $\textit{for the first time}$, use the UV luminosity function data from JWST and combine them with the $\textit{Planck}$ CMB data to probe neutrino self-interactions ($\nu$SI). If only one neutrino flavor experiences such BSM interactions, then $\textit{Planck}$ + JWST data give a 95% C.L. upper limit on $\mathrm{Log}_{10}(G_{\mathrm{eff}}/\mathrm{MeV}^{-2})$ $\approx$ $-2.75$ and when all three flavors are interacting, the corresponding constraint becomes $\lesssim -3.41$; both stronger than those obtained using only $\textit{Planck}$ data. Our results highlight the power of this new observable, the high-redshift UV luminosity function from JWST as a complementary probe to terrestrial experiments, showing that small-scale observables can open a new window onto smaller neutrino self-interaction strengths.
papers.reason: Combines Planck and JWST high-redshift UV luminosity functions to constrain BSM neutrino self-interactions modifying the matter power spectrum.

papers.title: General-relativistic neutrino-radiation hydrodynamics of crust ejection in magnetar giant flares
papers.abstract: Magnetar giant flares are thought to eject $\gtrsim 10^{-9}\,M_\odot$ of baryons, as inferred from the radio afterglow of the 2004 flare of SGR 1806-20. One proposed mechanism is a shock driven into the neutron-star crust by the hot, high-pressure layer that the flare creates above the surface. The unbound crust could undergo $r$-process nucleosynthesis and power a short-lived "nova brevis". We study this crust ejection with general-relativistic neutrino-radiation hydrodynamics simulations performed with AthenaK, using a tabulated nuclear equation of state and two-moment neutrino transport, for flare pressures corresponding to magnetic fields $B = 10^{15}$-$10^{16.5}$ G, and compute the nucleosynthesis of the ejecta with a nuclear reaction network. We find that such flares unbind $10^{-10}$ to $5\times10^{-8}\,M_\odot$ of crust. The ejecta keep the electron fraction of the crust to within a few hundredths, and weak interactions affect it mainly in the most energetic flares. The fast, high-entropy ejecta freeze out mostly as $\alpha$ particles and free neutrons. In the stronger flares nuclei up to the third $r$-process peak do form, but those with $A \geq 90$ make up at most $\approx 8\times10^{-4}$ of the ejected mass, or $\approx 3.5\times10^{-11}\,M_\odot$ per flare, and less than $10^{-5}$ for $B \leq 10^{15.5}$ G. A nova brevis from these ejecta would be powered mainly by the decay of free neutrons. Like earlier work, our models assume spherical symmetry, a flare that covers the whole star, and no magnetic field. A field tangential to the surface would hold the crust down and weaken the shock, and a flare confined to part of the surface should eject proportionally less mass. We therefore regard our ejecta masses as upper limits for a given flare pressure, and expect realistic magnetar flares to produce negligible amounts of $r$-process material.
papers.reason: Performs general-relativistic neutrino-radiation hydrodynamics simulations of crust ejection in magnetar giant flares and checks r-process nucleosynthesis.

papers.title: Exploring the limit of partonic collectivity in small collision systems at the LHC
papers.abstract: The existence of a partonic phase in small collision systems has been investigated previously through measurements of the elliptic flow ($v_{2}$) of mesons ($\pi^{\pm}$, K$^{\pm}$, and K$_{S}^{0}$) and baryons ($\rm{p}(\overline{\rm{p}})$, $\Lambda(\overline{\Lambda})$) in high-multiplicity p-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.02$ TeV and pp collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV recorded by ALICE. The results have revealed a grouping and splitting behavior of $v_{2}$ for baryons and mesons at intermediate transverse momentum ($p_{\rm{T}}$), establishing that partonic collectivity, as observed in heavy-ion collisions, is also present in these systems. In this Letter, the $p_{\rm{T}}$-differential $v_{2}$ of various hadronic species is investigated in p-Pb collisions for the multiplicity intervals $N_{\rm ch} \geq 50$, $25 \leq N_{\rm ch} < 50$, and $15 \leq N_{\rm ch} < 25$, as well as in pp collisions for $25 \leq N_{\rm ch} < 50$ and $15 \leq N_{\rm ch} < 25$. Here, $N_{\rm ch}$ is the efficiency-corrected number of charged particles produced in the kinematic region of $|\eta|< 0.8$ and $0.2 < p_{\rm T} < 3.0$ GeV/$c$. The characteristic mass dependence of $v_{2}$, as well as the grouping and splitting patterns among identified particles, are examined. The results in both p-Pb and pp collisions with $N_{\rm ch} \geq 25$ are consistent with the development of partonic collectivity. In the low-multiplicity region, $15 \leq N_{\rm ch} < 25$, the baryon-to-meson $v_{2}$ splitting, as quantified by the baryon-to-meson $v_2$ ratios, remains broadly consistent with that at higher multiplicities. However, its significance decreases to $\sim2\sigma$ in p-Pb collisions and to less than $1\sigma$ in pp collisions owing to the sizable experimental uncertainties. These measurements constitute the first steps towards identifying the limits of partonic flow in small collision systems at the LHC.
papers.reason: ALICE collaboration study of identified particle elliptic flow and partonic collectivity in small pp and p-Pb collision systems, relevant to generator multi-particle dynamics.

papers.title: Nuclear Atomic Dark Matter
papers.abstract: The matter coincidence, $\Omega_{\rm DM}\simeq5\Omega_b$, suggests a common origin for visible and dark matter (DM). We show that this motivates the study of nuclear atomic DM (naDM), which is composed of $\sim5\,\mathrm{GeV}$ mirror-neutron DM and a subdominant population of mirror elements. We realize naDM in the Mirror Twin Higgs, employing a twin Froggatt--Nielsen mechanism to generate fermion masses and realize spontaneous $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry breaking. However, the low-energy mirror framework is more general and can emerge from other ultraviolet completions. naDM gives rise to a novel two-stage dark acoustic oscillation signature, multiple correlated direct-detection signals, and highly exotic twin astrophysics.
papers.reason: Mirror-neutron dark matter with twin nucleon interactions, dark acoustic oscillations, and direct detection phenomenology.

papers.title: Enhancing Gravitational Waves from Global Strings via a First-Order Phase Transition
papers.abstract: We perform the first (3+1)-dimensional lattice simulations of a cosmological first-order phase transition (PT) in which true-vacuum bubbles with random phases nucleate, expand, and collide, producing a network of global strings. We find that the string network enters the scaling regime, and the coefficient of the logarithmic growth is smaller than the value obtained for a second-order PT. From the axion spectrum, we derive the dark-matter relic abundance and the dark-radiation bound from big bang nucleosynthesis on the axion decay constant $f_a$ and mass $m_a$. The ratio of the gravitational wave emission rate to the axion emission rate is found to be about two orders of magnitude larger than in the second-order case, and the resulting gravitational wave spectrum can be probed by pulsar timing arrays as well as by space- and ground-based interferometers.
papers.reason: Lattice simulations of cosmological first-order phase transitions producing global strings and axion/GW signals.

papers.title: Can cosmic neutrinos induce a cosmic birefringence signal?
papers.abstract: A coupling of photons to the cosmic neutrino asymmetry current has been proposed to explain the hinted isotropic rotation of CMB polarization. Gauge invariant UV completions require a Kalb-Ramond field that is exactly dual to a massless axion. We show that, in this case, the product of the axion-photon coupling and the axion-neutrino current coupling is fixed by the signal, $g_{a\gamma}/f_\ell=1/\Lambda_*^2$ with $\Lambda_*\simeq10$ TeV. Using $SU(2)_L$ gauge invariance we show that the dual axion couples to electrons as $g_{a\gamma}g_{ae}=m_e/\Lambda_*^2\simeq5\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. This value is excluded by the measured electron magnetic moment combined with light-shining-through-a-wall searches, as well as by stellar evolution. Conserved anomaly-free currents may evade these bounds, but then either a contact interaction among SM fermions excludes the model, or the relic neutrinos decouple from the signal. We conclude that cosmic neutrinos cannot induce a birefringence signal.
papers.reason: Examines whether cosmic neutrinos can induce cosmic birefringence via Kalb-Ramond/axion couplings, connecting neutrino backgrounds with precision cosmology.

papers.title: Search for dark matter axions at 1-2 micro-eV with a RADES-DarkQuantum haloscope at CERN
papers.abstract: The QCD axion remains one of the most compelling candidates for the dark matter of the Universe, yet the mass range around $1$\text{--}\SI{2}{\micro\electronvolt} remains essentially unexplored. In this paper, we describe a proposal to employ CERN's M1 superconducting magnet to deploy a haloscope to perform a search for galactic axion and axion-like particle dark matter providing continuous coverage from approximately 1.2 to 1.8 \SI{}{\micro\electronvolt}. Under conservative assumptions, the experiment can reach the QCD axion band over a significant fraction of the scanned range, while optimistic detector performance would allow sensitivity to benchmark models such as KSVZ and DFSZ over a large part of the explored mass interval. With the current long shut-down of CERN's accelerators providing a unique and timely window, such an experiment will deliver high-impact results even in conservative scenarios and potentially delivering a definitive test of the axion dark matter paradigm in the unexplored $1$\text{--}\SI{2}{\micro\electronvolt} mass range.
papers.reason: Axion dark matter search proposal using CERN magnet and haloscope technology in the 1-2 micro-eV range.

papers.title: Long lived MeV scale bound state dark matter alleviates the ${}^7 Li$ tension
papers.abstract: We investigate the impact of MeV scale unstable bound state dark matter on both thermal and non thermal Big Bang nucleosynthesis. Focusing on the weakly self interacting regime, we find that this framework can reproduce the theoretically predicted abundances through both short and long lived bound states. While long lived bound states can alleviate the cosmological ${}^7$Li problem, they simultaneously lead to discrepancies with other light element abundances. We show that this tension is resolved by incorporating non thermal nucleosynthesis, which act on these non standard initial light element abundances to alleviate the ${}^7 Li$ tension without violating observational constraints on the other elements. Remarkably, across the range of $\widetilde{\rho}_B$ and $m_\chi$ considered, long lived bound states with lifetimes $10^0\,{\rm s}\lesssim\tau\lesssim10^2\,{\rm s}$ can simultaneously resolve the ${}^7$Li problem and a large parameter space remain consistent with the observed abundances of the other light elements. Our results demonstrate that non thermal effects are essential for obtaining a consistent nucleosynthesis history in unstable bound state dark matter scenarios.
papers.reason: Explores unstable bound state dark matter and its non-thermal effects on Big Bang nucleosynthesis to alleviate the 7Li problem.

papers.title: Comparison of Methods for Extracting Three-Dimensional L\'evy Source Parameters in $\sqrt{s_{\text{NN}}} = 200\text{ GeV}$ Au+Au Collisions with EPOS3
papers.abstract: Bose--Einstein femtoscopy probes the spatiotemporal geometry of the particle-emitting source in heavy-ion collisions, where experimental data favor a L\'evy-stable source description. We compare four approaches for extracting 3D L\'evy source parameters using $\pi^+\pi^+$ pairs from EPOS3-simulated Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\text{NN}}} = 200\text{ GeV}$: direct fits to the pair-source distribution $D(\boldsymbol{\rho})$, and fits to the two-particle correlation function $C(\boldsymbol{q})$ obtained via (i) the CRAB package, (ii) direct numerical integration of $D(\boldsymbol{\rho})$, and (iii) fast Fourier transformation (FFT). On an identical momentum grid, numerical integration and FFT are analytically identical and numerically equivalent ($\text{RMSE} < 10^{-14}$), while FFT reduces the computation time from hours to seconds. We extract the transverse-mass dependence of the L\'evy radii, L\'evy index $\alpha$, and correlation strength $\lambda$ in $0\text{--}10\,\%$ central collisions. All methods reproduce the same physical trends, but CRAB results fluctuate due to event pooling, and correlation-function fits deviate systematically from direct source fits, e.g., with $\sim 7\text{--}9\,\%$ lower $\alpha$. These deviations may reflect residual non-L\'evy features of the source, probed differently in coordinate and momentum space, and the comparison of event-averaged parameters with fits to the ensemble-accumulated source, a mixture of L\'evy distributions with lower effective $\alpha$.
papers.reason: Compares methods for extracting 3D Lévy source parameters from Bose-Einstein femtoscopy in heavy-ion collisions.

papers.title: Testing the Spin of New Physics with Top Precision Measurements
papers.abstract: Precision measurements can reveal not only the presence of new physics, but also information about the dynamics that generated it. We study this question in top-pair production by comparing three top-philic scenarios: a colored scalar top partner, a colored vector-like fermion, and a spin-one $Z^\prime$ mediator. The first two contribute through loop corrections, while the $Z^\prime$ contributes at tree level. We show that the scalar and vector-like fermion scenarios match onto the same effective operator structure at low energies,making their distinction unfeasible using the EFT approach. However, near or above threshold their full loop amplitudes develop distinct momentum-dependent interference patterns. Using the top transverse momentum spectrum we find that resonant and loop-induced effects are relatively easy to distinguish, whereas separating the scalar and vector-like hypotheses is substantially more challenging. Nevertheless, their different analytic structures leave measurable information in the shape of the distribution. These results illustrate how precision differential measurements can probe the spin and dynamics of virtual new states even when they are not directly reconstructed, and motivate more powerful multidimensional analyses.
papers.topic: Top precision and new physics spin
papers.reason: Examines top-pair precision measurements to distinguish the spin of new physics mediators, aligning with precision EFT probes.

papers.title: Probing the Seed Effect of Supermassive Primordial Black Holes with Weak Gravitational Lensing
papers.abstract: We investigate the cosmological implications of supermassive primordial black holes (PBHs) as a component of dark matter (DM), focusing on their seed effect on large-scale structure formation. In contrast to the Poisson effect associated with the discrete distribution of PBHs, the seed effect arises because PBHs act as early gravitational seeds, accreting surrounding DM and developing dense DM spikes to form dressed PBHs. These structures enhance the matter power spectrum, particularly on small scales. We model their contribution within the halo-model framework under two prescriptions for DM accretion: an optimistic scenario (Case 1) and a conservative scenario (Case 2), which predict different modifications to the 1-halo term. We constrain the PBH abundance using weak-lensing measurements from the Dark Energy Survey Year 3 (DES Y3), performing a Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis to derive upper limits on the PBH fraction $f_{\rm PBH}$, as a function of the PBH mass $M_{\rm PBH}$. We find that weak lensing places competitive constraints on supermassive PBHs, with the upper limits on $f_{\rm PBH}$ becoming progressively stronger toward higher PBH masses. Case 1, which predicts more efficient DM accretion and hence a larger enhancement of the matter power spectrum, yields stronger constraints than Case 2; in particular, it excludes $f_{\rm PBH}\gtrsim10^{-4}$ for $M_{\rm PBH}\gtrsim10^{10} M_\odot$. We further forecast the sensitivity of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) using mock weak-lensing data and find that the constraints could improve by approximately two orders of magnitude. Our results establish weak gravitational lensing as a sensitive probe of the seed effect of supermassive PBHs and demonstrate its potential to complement other cosmological and astrophysical searches.
papers.reason: Constrains supermassive primordial black hole abundance using DES Y3 weak gravitational lensing via their seed effects on structure formation.

papers.title: Triaxial $\mu$-PIC for resolving Multi-Hit Ambiguity
papers.abstract: The micro pixel chamber ($\mu$-PIC), a type of micro-pattern gaseous detectors (MPGD), features pixel electrodes structured similarly to a sliced proportional counter. Conventionally, $\mu$-PIC electrodes are connected to orthogonal strip electrodes to reduce the number of readout circuits; however, this configuration introduces multi-hit ambiguity when tracing winding tracks or during high-rate operations. A well-known solution to this problem is the adoption of an additional readout axis. To this end, we designed a new electrode structure using Garfield++ simulations and fabricated a triaxial $\mu$-PIC based on through-glass-via (TGV) technology. This triaxial $\mu$-PIC achieved a high gas gain of $1.1\times 10^4$ and the energy resolution of 22\% (FWHM) at 5.9~keV, Furthermore, the false-hit probability was less than 0.78\% at a 95\% confidence level for two clusters separated by a distance of over 3 mm, consistent with Garfield++ predictions. With this triaxial $\mu$-PIC, single avalanche signals are collected from three independent readout strip electrodes (the anode and two cathodes). The charge ratio among these electrodes remains nearly constant at anode:U-cathode:V-cathode=3:2:1. In addition, we successfully achieved an enhanced gain of $3.2\times 10^4$ without increasing the discharge risk by employing an alternative operation mode.
papers.reason: Designs and tests a triaxial micro-pixel gaseous detector using TGV technology to resolve multi-hit ambiguities, relevant for gaseous TPCs.

papers.title: Stars Within Stars: The Interplay Between Main-Sequence Stars and Dark Matter
papers.abstract: Asymmetric dark matter may form self-gravitating macroscopic structures called dark stars if its microscopic properties give rise to sufficient effective pressure to counteract gravity. We study low-mass baryonic stars embedded within such dark stars, treating the baryonic and dark components as two gravitating fluids. The dark sector is assumed to be non-luminous and to interact with the baryonic star only through gravity, while the baryonic structure is computed using a realistic equation of state, opacity tables, and proton-proton-chain energy production. We find that the additional gravitational potential increases the luminosity at fixed baryonic mass, as the baryons must reach higher temperatures to maintain hydrostatic equilibrium. This lowers the minimum baryonic mass for hydrogen-burning configurations below the standard value of $\sim0.085M_\odot$. The resulting increase in luminosity can reduce the estimated main-sequence lifetime significantly, bringing low-mass configurations that would otherwise remain on the main sequence for hundreds of Gyr to cosmologically relevant timescales. We further show that photons escaping from the stellar surface undergo gravitational redshift determined by the global dark matter mass distribution. Consequently, extended dark star configurations can produce distinct observational signatures even when their outer regions have little effect on the intrinsic baryonic stellar structure, providing a potential probe of otherwise hidden dark structures.
papers.reason: Main-sequence stars embedded in asymmetric dark matter halos, touching on stellar evolution and dark matter.

papers.title: Natural Dark Matter in Generalized No-scale $\mathcal{F}$-$SU(5)$ at the HL-LHC and LUX-ZEPLIN Experiment
papers.abstract: Is a supersymmetric bulk region with sub-200 GeV neutralinos and right-handed sleptons still feasible? Initially the bulk was the discovery target of the supersymmetry (SUSY) pioneers in the 1980s, though reality crashed those ambitions over the subsequent years and decades, presumptively excluding these light neutralinos and sleptons, inviting finely tuned dark matter scenarios to satisfy emerging high-precision relic density measurements. The answer to this important question is $yes$, if we consider the GUT model $\mathcal{F}$-$SU(5)$, namely, flipped $SU$(5) supplemented with a string derived TeV-scale extra $10+\overline{10}$ vector-like multiplet and charged vector-like singlet $(XE,XE^c)$, dubbed flippons. We pair $\mathcal{F}$-$SU(5)$ with effective supernatural supersymmetry (SUSY), known as generalized No-Scale Supergravity (SUGRA). This merging of $\mathcal{F}$-$SU(5)$ with generalized No-Scale SUGRA solves the SUSY electroweak fine-tuning problem and includes natural dark matter (NDM) that meets the latest 5$\sigma$ Planck satellite observations through annihilation only. The NDM in this model is imminently under test by the LUX-ZEPLIN 1000-day experiment, thus prospective observed events by LUX-ZEPLIN in 2026-27 will compel confirmation by the high-luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) energizing in 2030. Therefore, we present the parameter space observable at both LUX-ZEPLIN and the HL-LHC that is consistent with all presently operating experiments, including the LHC Run 3 gluino and squark constraints. Our results predict sub-200 GeV neutralinos and right-handed sleptons in the bulk that are not beyond detection, though more massive electroweakinos greater than 600 GeV are also allowed.
papers.reason: Flipped SU(5) SUSY GUT with natural dark matter predictions for LZ and HL-LHC.

papers.title: Improved method for extracting low-energy expansion from OPE in mass-gapped theories
papers.abstract: Recently, Takaura proposed a new method for extracting the first nonzero coefficient of the low-energy expansion of an observable from its operator product expansion (OPE) in asymptotically free theories with a mass gap and a single threshold. The method uses a weight function to suppress the contribution of the ``duality-violation'' (DV) term that arises when relating the OPE to the low-energy expansion. We extend this method to low-energy expansion coefficients at arbitrary orders. We present two approaches: Method I uses weight functions that isolate the coefficients of low-energy expansion from the OPE. Method II subtracts the DV contribution from the OPE before the extraction. Applying these methods to the two-dimensional large-$N$ $O(N)$ nonlinear sigma model, we find that both methods successfully reconstruct higher-order low-energy expansion coefficients.
papers.reason: Improves extraction of low-energy expansion coefficients from OPE in mass-gapped theories using weight functions.

papers.title: Estimating Spectrum-Free Information Bounds for Generative Surrogates Beyond Conditional Collapse
papers.abstract: Conditional generative surrogates in high-energy physics, such as models that predict reconstructed jets from partons, are often evaluated on $1\text{D}$ marginal divergences among other metrics. Taken alone these metrics can reward conditional collapse. On a CMS simulation benchmark, a sampler that ignores the conditioner beats a trained Mixture Density Network (MDN) on all four target marginals under both KL and Wasserstein-1, and cannot be stably separated from a Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) model on two of the four. We instead score the models with the Continuous Ranked Probability Skill Score (CRPSS) from forecast verification, taking the exact marginal as the reference. We show how global skill depends on the evaluation spectrum, and we also report it within bins of a conditioning variable, where that dependence largely goes away. We then introduce a data-driven $k$-Nearest-Neighbor ($k$-NN) extrapolation that estimates the best CRPS the conditioning information allows. Both models agree with this estimate on all four targets, which suggests that current architectures have reached the information available in the conditioner, at least as far as these per-target scores can tell.
papers.reason: Evaluates conditional generative surrogates and metric information bounds for particle physics simulations.

papers.title: Phenomenological investigation of order statistics for multi-jet events
papers.abstract: We investigate rank-ordered jet rapidity distributions as probes of multijet radiation in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV. These observables retain information about the organization of jets within an event that is not resolved by the inclusive single-jet rapidity spectrum. We compare normalized predictions from the BFKL-based generator BFKLex and the collinear parton-shower generator PYTHIA 8.306, considering both fixed three-jet configurations and rank observables defined across multiplicities. We assess PDF and tune variations for PYTHIA 8.306, and PDF and factorization- and renormalization-scale variations for BFKLex. Total-variation and Wasserstein distances quantify the separation between the baseline shapes. Differences remain visible relative to the evaluated uncertainty bands in several well-populated regions. A minimum rapidity separation between the extremal jets modifies the discriminating power of the observables in a rank-dependent way. These results support rank-ordered rapidity spectra as experimentally accessible observables complementary to conventional Mueller-Navelet measurements for investigating high-energy QCD radiation.
papers.reason: Investigates rank-ordered jet rapidity distributions as probes of multijet QCD radiation.

papers.title: Has Quarkyonic Matter Been Seen in Lattice Simulations?
papers.abstract: Quarkyonic Matter refers to the dual state of matter between confined hadrons and quasi-free quarks. This duality leads to a robust constraint on the behavior of the distribution functions. After a comprehensive review of Quarkyonic Matter based on the distribution functions, we discuss recent lattice data for two-color QCD in $(1+1)$ and $(3+1)$ dimensions at finite baryon number density and QCD in $(3+1)$ dimensions at finite isospin density, as well as the astrophysically inferred equation of state. Taken together, these results reveal a coherent picture consistent with the emergence of Quarkyonic Matter in lattice simulations. Future lattice calculations of baryon and gauge-invariant quark momentum distributions at high density would provide a more direct test of this interpretation.
papers.reason: Reviews and analyzes lattice data for two-color and multi-dimensional QCD to identify quarkyonic matter, of adjacent interest for dense nuclear matter equations of state.

papers.title: Hypersurface covariance in relativistic local equilibrium
papers.abstract: Defining equilibrium typically requires specifying a three-dimensional spacelike hypersurface. While global equilibrium is hypersurface covariant, calculations involving local equilibrium can exhibit hypersurface dependence. In this work, we use polarization in heavy-ion collisions within the Zubarev response approach as an example to show that the hypersurface dependence arising from the local-equilibrium part of the density operator is canceled by an overlooked nondissipative contribution from its so-called ``dissipative part". We establish a hypersurface-covariant Zubarev framework for general geometries by consistently including both nondissipative and dissipative parts, eliminating dependence on the arbitrary hypersurface vector. The remaining frame dependence is physical: it arises from the medium rest frame entering the particle distribution and the time direction of the dissipative process, which usually coincide. This resolves, in principle, the longstanding and widely discussed conceptual disagreement over hypersurface dependence between two influential studies addressing the sign puzzles of $\Lambda$-hyperon polarization in heavy-ion collisions
papers.reason: Resolves hypersurface dependence and frame issues in relativistic local equilibrium and hyperon polarization for heavy-ion collisions.

papers.title: Parity-violating scalar-tensor theory revisited: complete basis up to $d=4$ and Hamiltonian analysis
papers.abstract: We construct complete bases of parity-violating generally covariant scalar-tensor (GST) and spatially covariant gravity (SCG) monomials up to derivative grade $d=4$. Including all derivative partitions, each description contains one $d=3$ and thirteen $d=4$ linearly independent monomials. At the level of Lagrangians, we find six integration-by-parts relations that reduce polynomial-type Lagrangians to combinations of one $d=3$ and seven $d=4$ monomials with general coefficient functions. We derive the correspondence between the two bases, retaining general coefficients and total derivatives, and establish their independence under integrations by parts. Among the seven $d=4$ SCG monomials, five contain neither the lapse velocity nor the time derivative of the extrinsic curvature. For the two remaining monomials, we perform a Hamiltonian constraint analysis with a standard Einstein-Hilbert kinetic term and a lapse-dependent potential. On the regular branches considered, the lapse-velocity term propagates four degrees of freedom (DOFs), while the extrinsic-curvature-velocity term propagates six DOFs, whether present alone or together with the lapse-velocity term. These results provide a complete basis for constructing parity-violating scalar-tensor theories with three DOFs up to $d=4$ within this setting, with the parity-violating Lagrangian spanned by six GST polynomials: one $d=3$ and five $d=4$ polynomials.
papers.reason: Constructs complete bases and Hamiltonian analyses of parity-violating scalar-tensor and spatial gravity theories up to derivative grade 4.

papers.title: To Infinity and Beyond: Maximizing Entanglement and Emergent Symmetries in $N$ Higgs Doublet Models
papers.abstract: In this paper, we explore the recent observation that maximizing flavor entanglement in Higgs boson scattering in a two Higgs doublet model leads to parameter space where the potential, if bounded from below, has an enhanced mirror symmetry $U(2)^2$. Looking at $N$ Higgs doublet models, we find a generalization of the mirror models, with $U(2)^N$ symmetry. Focusing on three Higgs doublet models, we determine that there is also a bounded potential solution that maximally entangles but has only the minimal $U(2)$ symmetry. This counterexample demonstrates that additional constraints must be imposed to maintain the connection between maximal entanglement and extended symmetries. As a potential constraint, for the three Higgs doublet model, we show that requiring maximal entanglement still occurs after gauging the symmetries eliminates the counterexample, thus restoring the connection.
papers.reason: Explores flavor entanglement in scalar potentials, touching on multi-Higgs models of peripheral interest.

papers.title: Amplitude Analysis of the Invariant-Mass Spectra of Centrally Exclusively Produced $\pi^+\pi^-$ and $K^+K^-$ Pairs in $pp$ Collisions at $\sqrt{s}=510$ GeV
papers.abstract: We present an amplitude analysis of the $\pi^{+}\pi^{-}$ and $K^{+}K^{-}$ invariant-mass spectra from central exclusive $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=510~\mathrm{GeV}$, measured by the STAR experiment with forward-scattered protons tagged in the Roman Pot detectors. The $\pi^{+}\pi^{-}$ channel is described with $f_{0}(500)$, $\rho^{0}(770)$, $f_{0}(980)$, $f_{2}(1270)$, $f_{0}(1500)$ and $f_{0}(1710)$ resonances with $\chi^{2}/\mathrm{ndf}=121.712/57$. The fit also yields $m_{f_{0}(980)}=0.989$ GeV and $\Gamma=0.091$ GeV. The $K^{+}K^{-}$ channel is described with $f_{0}(980)$, $f_{2}(1270)$, $f_{2}^{\prime}(1525)$ and $f_{0}(1710)$ resonances with $\chi^{2}/\mathrm{ndf}=14.662/15$. The fiducial cross sections for the individual resonances and interference terms were calculated, together with their ratios relative to the total fitted cross section. These ratios were compared across decay channels and qualitatively with previous measurements. A consistent flavor dependence of $f_{0}(1500)$ and $f_{0}(1710)$ has been derived for the highest RHIC collision energies, which is in agreement with low energy data.
papers.reason: Amplitude analysis of central exclusive pipi and KK production at RHIC, offering hadronic resonance data.

papers.title: First broadband search for fixed-polarization dark photon dark matter with GigaBREAD
papers.abstract: We present the first search for fixed-polarization dark photon (DP) dark matter in the 44-52$\mu\mathrm{eV}$ mass range, corresponding to 10.7-12.5GHz. GigaBREAD is a room-temperature broadband dish antenna experiment in which DP convert to ordinary photons on a cylindrical metallic emission surface and are focused onto a radio-frequency receiver. Previous searches, including GigaBREAD and several other dish antenna searches, have assumed randomly polarized DP dark matter. However, vector dark matter produced by a misalignment-like mechanism may retain an approximately fixed polarization, leading to sidereal modulation of the detector response as the Earth rotates. We reanalyze the GigaBREAD data using a polarization-matched likelihood that accounts for the time-dependent projection of a fixed DP polarization onto the detector axis.
